blocks.note: Choose mood and tense after expressions of possibility by separating the time of the event from the speaker's degree of commitment.
Turn direct commands, requests, permission, and prohibition into que clauses with a distinct subordinate subject.
Choose between an infinitive and a full que clause by tracking whether the two predicates share a subject.
Recast propositions as emotional reactions or value judgements without confusing presupposed truth with indicative assertion.
Read assertion, denial, and challenge in opinion clauses and negative questions before choosing indicative or subjunctive.
Complete factive and noun-led de que clauses according to whether the clause supplies information or sits inside an evaluation.
Select mood in clauses of purpose, cause, manner, and result, including the fixed remote comparison introduced by como si.
Contrast completed or habitual time clauses with pending future events and choose the corresponding subjunctive tense.
Frame conditions, exceptions, simultaneous events, and concessions as facts, open contingencies, or deliberately noncommittal cases.
Use mood in relative clauses to distinguish an identified referent from one sought, denied, hypothetical, or not yet established.
Integrate free-choice reduplication, wishes, and general subjunctive selectors while keeping time reference independent of mood.
